themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying tree complaints surged to 3 reports THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 380% spike—suggesting either a disease outbreak, storm damage, or neglect affecting the district's urban forest.
evidence: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% increase, z-score: 3.41)
No prior pattern suggests sudden environmental trigger—storm, disease, or maintenance failure
Aligns with waterfront development activity in Edgemere Commons and Arverne East, which could stress surrounding vegetation
reporting_angles: Did a recent nor'easter or storm damage trees? Interview Parks Department about damage assessments.
Is there a tree disease or pest outbreak in Far Rockaway? Check with Dept. of Environmental Protection.
Are recent development projects (Edgemere Commons Phase 2B, Arverne East) cutting or destabilizing mature trees?

themes_detail.label: Street Light Failures Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints jumped to 38 reports LAST WEEK, up 171% from a baseline of 14 per week over 8 weeks, indicating a sudden outbreak of outages or maintenance gaps that could compromise safety in an already underserved waterfront community.
evidence: 38 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 14 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (171% spike, z-score: 4.62, severity: high)
Far Rockaway historically has lower streetlight coverage than NYC average, making outages disproportionately visible
Safety implications for residents walking at night, especially near industrial/waterfront areas
reporting_angles: Map the 38 complaints LAST WEEK geographically—are outages clustered in one neighborhood or transit corridor?
Interview DOE about why this week saw a spike. Is there a specific cause (aging infrastructure, power grid issue)?
Speak to residents about how lighting outages affect perceived safety and nighttime mobility.

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints exploded to 4 complaints 3 weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 3,100% spike with a z-score of 11.72—marking the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset and suggesting a potentially serious contamination or supply issue.
evidence: 4 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3,100% increase, z-score: 11.72—the single highest anomaly in dataset)
Related spikes in Plumbing (247 complaints, 90-day aggregate) and Water System (261 complaints) suggest systemic water infrastructure stress
No recent news coverage identified; potential underreported public health concern
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to request water quality test results and any advisories issued 3 weeks ago. Was there a boil water notice?
Interview affected residents about what they observed (discoloration, odor, taste) and how it impacted them.
Investigate whether water main breaks or aging pipes in Far Rockaway (historically older infrastructure) are the root cause.

themes_detail.label: Noise—Commercial & Street/Sidewalk
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints spiked 231% LAST WEEK (12 vs. 3.6 weekly average), while street/sidewalk noise surged 154% LAST WEEK (40 vs. 15.8 weekly average), together suggesting either new construction, a commercial venue, or event activity disrupting quiet hours.
evidence: Commercial noise: 12 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.6 weekly average (231% spike, z-score: 6.36)
Street/Sidewalk noise: 40 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 15.8 weekly average (154% spike, z-score: 3.73)
DOB data shows 410 new permits filed in 90 days (234 alterations, 146 new buildings), indicating active construction that may correlate with noise complaints
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 noise complaints LAST WEEK with DOB permits and active construction sites—are they co-located?
Is a new bar, restaurant, or entertainment venue operating without proper noise mitigation or Department of Environmental Protection approval?
Interview residents about timing (early morning, late night, weekends) and sources. Are contractors violating noise regulations?

themes_detail.label: Damaged Street Signs Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints jumped to 21 reports 2 weeks ago, a 630% spike from a baseline of 2.9 per week—indicating either weather damage, vehicular accidents, or systematic neglect of wayfinding infrastructure.
evidence: 21 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (630% spike, z-score: 10.72)
Timing suggests potential weather event (nor'easter, heavy winds) 2–3 weeks ago that knocked out signs across the district
No follow-up complaints in most recent week suggest either issue was addressed or reporting subsided
reporting_angles: Verify whether a storm event 2–3 weeks ago damaged street signage. Cross-check with National Weather Service records.
Check DOT's repair response time—how quickly were damaged signs replaced or repaired?
Interview residents about wayfinding impact, especially in areas with high pedestrian or vehicle confusion.
